name: Password hash with insufficient computational effort
description:
The application hashes passwords with a scheme that costs an attacker almost nothing per guess: a fast general-purpose hash (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512 and the like) applied once and without a salt, or bcrypt with a cost factor below 10. A stolen digest of this kind is attacked offline at millions to billions of guesses per second on commodity hardware, and without a salt identical passwords share a digest and precomputed tables apply.

burpsy reports this only on proof: for a password parameter it found, in the answer, the exact digest it computed of the password it sent (a random marker confirmed by a second one, or the submitted value of a replayed login with working credentials, absent from the answer to a random marker), or a bcrypt hash that bcrypt itself verifies against the submitted value with a cost factor below 10.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no entry for it.
remediation: Store passwords with Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt (cost 10 or more, raised as hardware improves) or PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with at least 600,000 iterations, each with a unique random salt. Never return a password hash to the client.
